## Data dictionary review checklist

- [ ] Dataset version, date received, dimensions, source, and unit are recorded.
- [ ] Every table has a grain and key.
- [ ] Every source and derived variable has one dictionary row.
- [ ] Definitions explain business meaning rather than repeat names.
- [ ] Types, formats, units, allowed values, and examples are clear.
- [ ] Missing-value codes and counts are documented, including zero missingness.
- [ ] Constraints, relationships, derivations, and ownership are recorded.
- [ ] Privacy or sensitivity classifications are visible.
- [ ] The dictionary matches the final analytical data.

## EDA report outline

1. purpose, questions, and scope;
2. source data, versions, and units of analysis;
3. data-quality findings and decisions;
4. cleaning, transformation, and feature engineering;
5. selected univariate findings;
6. purposeful bivariate findings;
7. relevant multivariate findings;
8. limitations and unresolved issues;
9. conclusions and project implications; and
10. dictionary, references, code, and reproducibility information.

## Interim review checklist

- [ ] The current problem, audience, and scope are clear.
- [ ] Completed, preliminary, and planned work are distinguished.
- [ ] Progress is supported by observable evidence.
- [ ] Data issues, open questions, and risks are visible.
- [ ] Model and projection plans include validation.
- [ ] Project trajectory is supported by the schedule.
- [ ] Feedback and decision requests are specific.
- [ ] Next actions have owners and dates.

## Final report revision audit

- [ ] The executive summary leads with findings and actions.
- [ ] Every major section advances the same decision problem.
- [ ] Main EDA findings are integrated into the report body.
- [ ] Segment descriptions separate observations from assumptions.
- [ ] Forecasts, projections, scenarios, and targets are labelled correctly.
- [ ] Recommendation effects are not presented as measured outcomes without evidence.
- [ ] Secondary comparisons use compatible definitions and denominators.
- [ ] Machine-learning results include a baseline, validation, and useful metrics.
- [ ] Figures remain legible at final size.
- [ ] Repetition and nonessential detail have been removed.

## Final deliverable checklist

- [ ] Reported values reconcile with the analysis.
- [ ] The report and presentation share the same conclusions.
- [ ] Recommendations are supported, feasible, and measurable.
- [ ] Limitations and assumptions are visible.
- [ ] Figures and tables are labelled, sourced, and accessible.
- [ ] Appendices provide necessary technical support.
- [ ] The executive summary stands alone.
- [ ] Presentation timing, transitions, participation, and questions have been rehearsed.
- [ ] Confidentiality requirements are satisfied.
- [ ] Handoff files are documented, clearly named, and usable.
